title: Halal and Haram: How Do We Ask When We Don't Know the Ruling?
summary:
At this age, your child may ask: why is this permitted and that forbidden? Start with a specific reference instead of inventing an explanation for every ruling. Permitted and prohibited matters here refer to wholesome and impure things in Al-A'raf 7:157. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ ٱلۡأُمِّيَّ ٱلَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُۥ مَكۡتُوبًا عِندَهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ يَأۡمُرُهُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَىٰهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡخَبَـٰٓئِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنۡهُمۡ إِصۡرَهُمۡ وَٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِهِۦ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُۥٓ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ﴾ [Surah Al-A'raf: 157] (interpretation of the meaning: "Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him – it is those who will be the successful"). This is a specific Qur'anic reference, not a detailed ruling list for every food or toy.

Suggest a simple situation: your child asks about a new food or toy. Say: «Let's understand the question first: what is the food or toy, and what concerns you about it?» Write down the details. Do not decide a ruling from a name alone or guess the wisdom behind it. The aim is to help parent and child frame the question before seeking an answer.

The second Qur'anic reference is an-Nahl 16:43, concerning asking ahl adh-dhikr when one does not know, within a discussion of the messengers. Referring fiqh questions we cannot answer to people of knowledge is the application's own policy; the application issues no fatwas.

If you do not know the answer, say calmly: «I don't know the ruling; we will put the question to people of knowledge instead of my guessing.» Record the question, the answer, and the scholar or body who gave it for future reference. Avoid calling every small mistake haram when you do not know the ruling. Honesty about what you know and do not know beats guessing.
try_this: Today: Write down one question with your child about a real situation, its details and what you do not know about it. If you do not know the ruling, prepare the question for people of knowledge instead of guessing an answer.
reflection_prompts: When you do not know the ruling on something your child asks about, do you say so and prepare the question together for people of knowledge, or try to answer by guessing?
parent_script: “My little one, always remember that when we don't know the ruling on a matter, we ask the people of knowledge so that we may learn what is correct.”
assistant_prompts: How can I explain to my 8-year-old child the importance of asking scholars about Islamic rulings instead of guessing?
What practical activities can I do with my child to train them to formulate Islamic questions and present them to people of knowledge?
